identity.trusted_rule: every row carrying the USEF number attaches unconditionally (plan rule 3) — including a zero-padded twin registration

horses.detail: not one of the horses on your USEF-anchored record

rules.usef_trusted: plan rule 3 — the record carries the USEF number, so every row on it attaches unconditionally
rules.horse_name_bridge: plan rule 5 — an exact-name, name-only record rode a horse whose NAME is on the trusted side, and no other registered person with the same name rode a horse of that name
rules.horse_name_bridge_verified: plan rule 5, verified-rider branch — the caller supplied the USEF number or confirmed that USEF identity, and the name-only row names a horse already on that rider's trusted record. A conflicting non-empty horse registry id still blocks
rules.horse_registry_id_bridge_verified: plan rule 5, verified-rider branch — the caller supplied or confirmed the USEF identity and the name-only horse carries a registry id on that trusted record
rules.horse_typo_bridge_verified: plan rule 5, verified-rider typo branch — the caller supplied or confirmed the USEF identity, the trusted rider already rode the matched horse, and the pool spelling differs from exactly one trusted horse by only whitespace or one edit. Short names, appended suffixes, ambiguous hubs, and conflicting registry ids are never auto-attached
rules.answered_yes: plan rule 6 — attached only because an answer said yes
rules.horse_name_variant_trip_confirmed: auto-attached under the FULL conjunction: a pairwise name-variant relation to one of the rider's own horses (cores that drop at most one short edge token, a whitespace squash, or a near spelling — never transitive, never a global index), AND same-trip evidence (same day, same class code, same finishing position, containing class titles) whose DOMINANT target is that same horse, AND that horse not being contested by another registered person with this exact name — contest status is INHERITED by the variant — AND the candidate having passed the exact person-name gate. Attached at ROW level, only rows ridden by the confirmed candidate. Neither half is safe alone: names alone link 67,106 pairs of provably different animals, trips alone are ~37% precise
rules.contested: not attached: another USEF-registered person with the same exact name also competed a horse of that name, so it is asked, never assumed
rules.near_miss: not attached: the horse name is a near spelling of one of yours. An APPENDED near miss (base + a trailing run, e.g. DEGENHARDT 5) can never auto-attach at all, because a trailing numeral is an FEI homonym disambiguator; a one-edit typo can auto-attach only after the rider's USEF identity is verified and exactly one horse already on that trusted record is the typo target
rules.unknown_horse: not attached: the horse is not on the trusted side at all
rules.unverified_name: not attached: this record reached the candidate set through the ingest's merge_candidates hint rather than exact-name equality, so rule 5's premise does not hold for it and no other registered person with ITS name could have contested the horse
rules.identity_confirmed: feature D — no USEF number was typed, so the keyed anchor is an inference from a NAME. One confirmation question naming that record's most-ridden horse was asked and answered YES; the record then attaches under rule 3's own terms. A NO rejects the record and the run re-resolves without it, and an UNANSWERED question attaches nothing at all
rules.name_resolved_anchor: the anchor carries no USEF/FEI number. It is a name-only catalog row, i.e. a NAME BUCKET rather than a human, so it is NOT trusted: every horse on it is asked about exactly like a pool record's (rules 5/6), and rows attach only on an answer
rules.unanchored_pool: not attached: there is no USEF-anchored record in this run at all, so nothing corroborates any horse and each one has to be claimed. Owner's rule, 2026-07-29: "for non usef people we should ask about every horse"

rows.detail: these rows carry no horse name, so the rider has no useful evidence to verify them; they stay excluded without creating a question

anchor_identity_confirmation.why: no USEF number was given, so the keyed record was chosen by NAME alone and had to be confirmed before anything on it attached

rules.usef_id_in_name: one record's NAME quotes the other's USEF competition id ('2025 ESP Pre-Charity (#316789/343747)'), and the spans overlap. A source asserting both ids in one name is asserting they are one event, so the two ids become ALIASES rather than being refused by the usef_comp_id invariant
rules.no_date_overlap: APART — the spans share no day. 0 SAME / 19 DIFF, and not one such pair shares a single ride. This one requirement kills all seven of the wrong merges today's pipeline makes (MADE IN THE SHADE I/II/III are three separate USEF competitions on three consecutive days)
rules.month_span_record_no_ride_evidence: APART — a span longer than 14 days with no shared ride at all is a synthetic whole-month blob (equestrian_digital_nameonly, 18/18 of its records). 44/44 correctly kept apart, 0 SAME lost
rules.different_usef_competition_id: APART — two different numeric USEF competition ids are two USEF-licensed competitions. Capital Challenge runs one physical event under 1023 (Hunter/Jumper) and 279067 (Equitation); Split Rock runs a national and a CSI2* the same week. Merging those fabricates a competition the USEF record does not contain
rules.identical_name_over_usef_id: the ids differ but the normalised name TOKENS are identical — a genuine USEF duplicate record (2024 LAS VEGAS NATIONAL is 344618 and 345490). This and usef_id_in_name are the only two rules that may declare two ids ALIASES of one licensed event; the alias is applied before the closure and listed in `usef_id_aliases`. Every other pair of differing ids is still refused outright
rules.two_shared_rides: two identical rides (class code + title + horse + placing) on overlapping days: 168/168 SAME, at any date gap. ONE shared ride also merges, but only on an identical START DATE — see same_start_date_shared_ride
rules.horse_in_both_on_one_day: ASK — the same horse appears in both records on the same recorded CLASS DATE, but some source lanes reuse or corrupt that date across several differently named shows. The date alone is corroboration, not proof
rules.identical_show_name: identical stop-word-stripped, roman-normalised name tokens WITH span overlap: 78/78 SAME. Without the overlap requirement it is 78/80 — DRESSAGE AT KIRBY HILL (8/3) and DRESSAGE AT KIRBY HILL FARM (8/2) are different shows whose tokens are identical because FARM is a stop word
rules.four_shared_class_horse: four shared (class code, horse) pairs inside a sane span with no state conflict: 165/165 SAME
rules.same_start_date_shared_ride: an identical START DATE plus at least one identical ride (class code + horse + placing), no state conflict and no contradicted placing: 90/90 SAME over 36 riders. Restricted to gap == 0 because that is where the evidence lives — at trips == 1 the whole labelled band is 33 SAME / 2 DIFF and BOTH DIFF pairs are off-date (BLUE ROCK vs MAGIC HILL SPRING FESTIVAL 7 at gap 4; TEXAS ROSE SUMMER BREED vs TEXAS ROSE WELSH LITE at gap 1). This rule exists because the ordering without it was non-monotonic in evidence: at gap == 0 with a similar name, ZERO shared rides merged via same_start_date_same_name and TWO merged via two_shared_rides, but exactly ONE fell through to an ASK — so adding a corroborating ride made the pipeline less willing to merge
rules.one_shared_ride: ASK — exactly one identical ride and the start dates DIFFER. The gap-0 case merges above; what is left is the co-located dual-licence case (Split Rock national vs CSI2*), which is normally caught earlier by different_usef_competition_id and only reaches here when one side carries no USEF id
rules.same_start_date_same_name: identical START DATE, no state conflict, name sequence ratio >= 0.75. Measured on the honest hard set (identical start, no shared ride): seq < 0.70 is 0/13 SAME, seq >= 0.80 is 12/12 SAME, and [0.70, 0.80) is EMPTY. The nearest DIFF is OCALA SPRING PREMIERE I vs WEC OCALA SPRING 1 at 0.68 — two Ocala showgrounds, one week
rules.same_name_conflicting_state: ASK — same start date and name, but the normalised states disagree. 2 SAME / 32 DIFF; both SAME are 2024 Las Vegas National, filed CA by SGL and NV by USEF
rules.same_class_same_horse_placings_differ: ASK — starts within a day and the same horse in the same class in both, with different recorded placings on the two sides (both real values: a blank is not a disagreement). Fully absorbed by the rules above on ground truth, so it has NO measured precision and must never be promoted to a merge
rules.same_class_same_horse: ASK — starts within a day and the same horse in the same class in both, and the two records do not CONTRADICT each other (one of them simply records no placing, which is what the entries-only lanes ship). Split out of the rule above, which used to fire here too and then told the rider their two records 'disagree' about a placing that was identical, or printed a literal None. Same verdict, honest sentence
rules.no_shared_ride: APART — nothing above fired. Name similarity is disallowed entirely once the start dates differ: at gap >= 1 with no shared ride, seq 0.9-1.0 is 1 SAME / 17 DIFF and every lower band is 0 SAME. There is no cut

_meta.deduplication: APPLIED, after attachment. Rule 7 governs ATTACHMENT — no record is ever refused for looking like a duplicate — and this document is the clean view of everything that attached. Duplicate trips are suppressed only when a richer row proves the replacement; the authoritative usef lane is never suppressed; every suppressed row is enumerated in _audit.deduplication and donates its unique fields to the row that replaced it. _audit.reconciled proves emitted + suppressed == attached.
_meta.showMerge: APPLIED: a pairwise decision then a union-find closure. Same dates create a strong presumption and RIDE evidence discharges it — identical start date WITH a shared ride is 99.2% one show, WITHOUT one it is 50%. Merged on: a USEF id quoted in the other name, TWO shared rides, one horse in both on one class date, identical normalised name tokens, four shared (class, horse) pairs, or an identical start date with a name sequence ratio >= 0.75 and no state conflict. Every merge requires the spans to OVERLAP, no merge uses name similarity once the start dates differ, and two different numeric USEF competition ids are never united. Genuinely uncertain pairs are ASKED (see openShowQuestions) and default to staying apart. Venue/city aliases are NOT merged.

_meta.horseQuestionClustering: Horse questions are grouped per ANIMAL, not per spelling: one question per cluster, rows summed, every spelling named, and three answers — true, false, or "split" (these are different horses, ask me one at a time). The printed list is capped by CLUSTER and the cap is disclosed (questions_omitted + rows_omitted_from_printed_questions).

_meta.identityGate: APPLIED. Without a USEF number the anchor is an INFERENCE, so it is not exempt from the horse test that has always governed the pool. A keyed anchor chosen by name costs ONE confirmation question naming its most-ridden horse (true proceeds, false rejects the record and re-resolves, unanswered attaches nothing); a NAME-ONLY anchor is a name BUCKET, not a human, so it is put through rules 5/6 whole — every horse asked, per animal, nothing attached until answered.
